message.content: You know how the VHS CLI recording program exists? What if we created something like that for agentic chat sessions—to prove out agent skills, workflows, prompting techniques, and MCPs visually for people?

This feels like VHS + Playwright Trace Viewer + an eval harness for agent sessions. It shouldn’t merely screen-record a chat; it should capture the agent’s execution as a reproducible, inspectable artifact.
Not hard to prove, moderately hard to make useful, genuinely hard to make universal and trustworthy. A compelling trace-to-HTML prototype is a one-to-two week project.
Couldn’t we simply snapshot the chat artifact to replay it?
Exactly. If the goal is visual demonstration, snapshotting the chat artifact is probably the right first product. The renderer simply rehydrates events according to their timestamps.

event.content: Surveyed AgentReplay, Tracehouse, Traces, Hugging Face Agent Traces, Retrace, and Microsoft Foundry Trace Replay.

message.content: The primitive exists. The opening is a VHS-quality authoring experience: an editable tape, polished exports, instructional captions, and verifiable assertions.
The niche/use case I have is for documentation visuals and learning materials, if that matters.
That matters enormously. You’re not building agent observability. You’re building a documentation renderer for agent sessions: turn a real session into a polished, maintainable visual lesson.
Could you build a prototype of this? Maybe even use this exact chat session as the first artifact lol.
